title: Jerusalem, A Useless Vine

questions.question: What wood does the Lord ask Ezekiel about, asking how it is better than any other wood?
options: The wood of the olive tree
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:2 (ESV): "Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?"

questions.question: What practical question is asked to show the uselessness of vine wood?
options: "Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?"
"Can it be carved into a bow?"
"Will it serve as a pillar for a house?"
"Can you make a wheel from its branch?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:3 (ESV): "Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?"

questions.question: To what is the wood of the vine given for fuel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 (ESV): "Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel."

questions.question: When the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, what question is asked?
options: "How long until it turns to ash?"
"Can it be plucked from the fire?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 (ESV): "when the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, is it useful for anything?"

questions.question: If the vine was not useful for anything when it was whole, how much less when...?
options: ...the fire has consumed it and it is charred!
...it is plucked up by the roots!
questions.correctAnswer: ...the fire has consumed it and it is charred!
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:5 (ESV): "Behold, when it was whole, it was used for nothing. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it ever be used for anything!"

questions.question: Who does the Lord compare the wood of the vine to?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:6 (ESV): "Therefore thus says the Lord God: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem."

questions.question: What does God say He will set against the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 (ESV): "And I will set my face against them."

questions.question: What is the inescapable nature of their judgment according to verse 7?
options: Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them
Though they hide in the mountains, the sword will find them
If they flee from the sword, the lion will devour them
Even if they build high walls, the earthquake will break them down
questions.correctAnswer: Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 (ESV): "Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them."

questions.question: What will the people know when God sets his face against them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:7 (ESV): "and you will know that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them."

questions.question: Why will God make the land desolate?
options: Because they refused to pay tribute
Because they did not celebrate the Jubilee
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:8 (ESV): "And I will make the land desolate, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord God."

questions.question: In the analogy of the vine branch, what is its only purpose since it cannot be used for timber?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 (ESV): "Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel."

questions.question: The metaphor of the vine represents Israel's standing among what?
options: The trees of the forest (the nations)
questions.correctAnswer: The trees of the forest (the nations)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:2 (ESV): "...the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?" The trees often represent other nations, and Israel the vine.

questions.question: A vine is generally known for producing what? (Though chapter 15 emphasizes its worthless wood).
questions.explanation: A vine's only value is its fruit. If it bears no fruit, its wood is useless for building, only good for burning.

questions.question: What part of the useless vine had the fire consumed?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4 (ESV): "when the fire has consumed both ends of it..."

questions.question: What does "the middle of it is charred" signify about Jerusalem?
options: It is already partially destroyed and weak, unfit for anything
It will survive the coming war
It is being refined like silver
It is protected by God's hand
questions.correctAnswer: It is already partially destroyed and weak, unfit for anything
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 15:4-5 points out that since it was charred already, it is even more useless. Jerusalem had already suffered previous sieges and deportations, making its remaining state weak and fit only for total destruction.

key_verse_text: "And I will set my face against them. Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them; and you will know that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them."
